title: EngineForge Early Access is now open
author: Plastic_Bag6171
selftext:
Hey all,

EngineForge Early Access is now open.

We’ve been building EngineForge, a VS Code fork made specifically for game development, and we’re finally putting it in front of real developers.

EngineForge automatically indexes your project into a code graph that understands your files, scripts, scenes, dependencies, and relationships, so the AI agent has more context before it starts helping.

From there, it can connect to your engine in real time, write and modify code, create objects and nodes, attach scripts, inspect errors, and make changes directly inside your Unity or Godot project.

What you get in Early Access:

• $20 of free usage to explore EngineForge    
• Full AI Agent usage    
• Unity 2021.3+ support    
• Godot 4.0+ support    
• Asset Store access for browsing and adding free assets    
• Early access to a game dev focused AI workflow  

This is still an early alpha, so we expect bugs, rough edges, and things that can be improved. That’s exactly why we’re opening it up now.

We’re looking for feedback from game developers of all experience levels, whether you’ve shipped games before, are working on your first project, or are just curious about AI-assisted game development.

You can try it now or read more here:

https://engineforge.ai

Would love to hear what you think.

comments.author: KingAster
comments.body: Amazing project. What if I have a separate Codex/Claude subscription? Can I use it?

replies.author: Plastic_Bag6171
replies.body:
Thanks a lot!

Not at the moment. Right now, EngineForge uses Claude through our own integration, so separate Codex or Claude subscriptions are not supported yet.

It’s something we may consider later, but for now everything runs through EngineForge directly.

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body:
1. How's it different from using codex with a codebase?
2. Can I use other AI & local with it?

replies.author: Plastic_Bag6171
replies.body:
EngineForge is different because it’s not only codebase-aware, it’s engine-aware.

It connects to Unity/Godot, understands scenes, objects, nodes, logs, and can make changes inside the engine, not just edit code.



Right now we use Claude through our own integration. Other providers / local models are not available yet, but we’re considering it.

replies.author: GentlemenBehold
replies.body: How does it connect to Unity?

replies.author: Plastic_Bag6171
replies.body:
It connects through a local Unity bridge plugin.

Once you open the Unity project with EngineForge, the AI agent can communicate directly with the Unity Editor, not only writing code, but also creating/modifying GameObjects, attaching scripts, changing scene properties, and reading console errors.

Everything runs locally against your Unity project.
